title: Prepare and install a patch to repair an aircraft or component
subject: Airframe

sheetSections.name: Flush patches need a doubler to attach to under the skin

assumptions: Set shank and spring are undamaged, clean and free of burrs, mushrooming or chipping on the working face.
Protruding shank length is sufficient to form a shop head of about 0.5D height and 1.5D width.
The workpiece was backed/supported so the blow drove the shank out rather than deflecting the sheet.

Shop head dimensions measured on every driven rivet — height and width recorded against the rivet shank diameter — plus recorded finished hole diameter and the gauge/alloy of doubler and filler stock.
openQuestions: Every check, error mode and evidence item in this pack was drafted by packs/compile_pack.py from the procedure sheet and handbook, and has not been reviewed by a subject-matter expert.

Does this practical require a flush patch (doubler plus filler, as the procedure sheet's fabrication steps assume) or a lap/scab patch? The handbook edge-distance and 1"/staggered 1/2" spacing figures on p. 4-96 are stated for the lap patch and may not govern a flush patch layout.
What skin thickness and alloy is the training coupon, and what rivet diameter, edge distance and pitch does that yield? Without these the layout criteria cannot be checked numerically.
What tolerance band applies to the campus 0.5D/1.5D shop head figures — the sheet says 'preferred' but gives no accept/reject range.
Is the source of the rivet count an SRM, AC 43.13-1 Figure 4-169, or an instructor-supplied value? The pack currently accepts 'the documented calculation'.

Is the Remove the Rivet section graded on the same coupon as the installed patch, or on a separate practice piece? This changes whether a vacated hole in the finished patch is a defect or expected evidence.

subtasks.label: Identify the Damage
subtasks.excluded: 2 [video], 2 [document], 3 [measurement] — held beside the frame, never folded into the criterion.

steps.text: Inspect the area for damage.

checks.text: Dirt, grease and paint are removed from the damaged area and surrounding structure so each rivet and fastener is visible.
checks.src: Handbook: "Remove all dirt, grease, and paint from the damaged and surrounding areas to determine the exact condition of each rivet, bolt, and weld."

checks.text: Inspection extends into the adjacent area, covering skin wrinkles, dents, loose rivets and abrasions, not just the obvious damage.
checks.src: Handbook: "Inspect skin for wrinkles throughout a large area" and "Check all skin, dents, and wrinkles for any cracks or abrasions."

checks.text: Any movable parts in the inspected area are operated and confirmed to function normally.
checks.src: Handbook: "Check the operation of all movable parts in the area."

checks.text: Damage type is named and classified, with a stated determination that repair rather than replacement is appropriate.
checks.src: Handbook: "Determine if repair would be the best procedure"; damage classes given on p.4-90.

errors.text: Inspection stops at the visible damage; cracks, working rivets or wrinkles in adjacent structure go unfound.
Damage misclassified as negligible or patchable when it exceeds limits, so the wrong repair path is started.
Area left dirty, greasy or painted, hiding fine cracks and fretting residue around rivet heads.

steps.text: Measure the extent of the damage.

checks.text: Recorded height and length capture the full extent of the damage, including crack tips and adjacent affected area.
checks.src: Handbook: "the extent of damage must be fully evaluated" and "Check all skin, dents, and wrinkles for any cracks or abrasions."

checks.text: A steel scale rests flat on the surface, spanning the damage's greatest dimension with its zero at the damage edge.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note 1: "Use a steel scale to find the damage's height and length."

checks.text: The damaged and surrounding area is free of dirt, grease and loose paint so the damage boundary is unambiguous.
checks.src: "Remove all dirt, grease, and paint from the damaged and surrounding areas to determine the exact condition".

checks.text: Measured dimensions are compared against the permissible damage limits for that component before a repair class is chosen.
checks.src: "Permissible limits for negligible damage vary for different components of different aircraft and should be carefully researched on an individual basis."

errors.text: Only the visibly obvious damage is measured; crack ends or adjacent distortion are excluded, understating the extent.
Dimensions estimated by eye or with the scale skewed/not zeroed, yielding wrong height and length.
Measurements taken but not written down, so layout later relies on memory.

steps.text: Mark the repair area with a marker around all of the damage.

checks.text: The marker outline fully encircles the damage, with every crack tip, dent edge and abrasion inside the line.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: mark "around all of the damage"; handbook 4-92 "Remove all distorted skin and structure in damaged area."

checks.text: The outline is circular or oval, or if rectangular has visibly rounded rather than square corners.
checks.src: Handbook: "try to make cutouts either circular or oval in shape"; also p.4-92 "Round all square corners."

checks.text: Rectangular marked corners carry a radius of no less than 1/2 inch.
checks.src: Handbook: "make the radius of curvature at each corner no smaller than 1/2-inch" for rectangular cutouts.

checks.text: The marked boundary lies outside the measured damage extent by a clear margin on all sides, in sound metal.
checks.src: Compare outline to the height/length taken with the steel scale; handbook 4-92: edges of completed repair match existing structure.

errors.text: Outline drawn on or inside the damage boundary, leaving crack tips or distortion outside the removal area.
Repair area marked with sharp square corners, creating a stress-riser cutout when cut.
Boundary scribed or scratched into the skin instead of marked, or line so heavy it hides the damage.

subtasks.excluded: 2 [measurement], 1 [video] — held beside the frame, never folded into the criterion.

steps.text: Cut out or stop the damage from spreading.

checks.text: No crack, tear or distorted material remains inside the cut perimeter; the damage is fully excised or arrested.
checks.src: Handbook p.4-92 damage removal: "Remove all distorted skin and structure in damaged area"; procedure sheet step 1.

checks.text: A stop hole 3/32-inch diameter is drilled at each crack end so the hole encloses the crack tip.
checks.src: Handbook p.4-96 figure: "Stop holes—drill 3/32" diameter holes in each sharp corner"; p.4-93 "a small hole must be drilled in each end".

checks.text: The cutout is circular/oval or has rounded corners — no square corners remain in the opening.
checks.src: "Round all square corners"; p.4-86 "try to make cutouts either circular or oval in shape", rectangular corner radius "no smaller than 1/2-inch" (measured separately).

checks.text: Surrounding skin outside the marked repair area is free of saw skips, gouges or overcuts.
checks.src: Handbook p.4-92: "Remove damaged material so that the edges of the completed repair match existing structure and aircraft lines."

subtasks.excluded: 6 [measurement], 2 [video] — held beside the frame, never folded into the criterion.

steps.text: Transfer the opening’s shape.

checks.text: The traced outline on the blank reproduces the opening's full perimeter as one continuous fine line, with no gaps, double lines or corner deviation.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "Use a fine-tip marker to trace the shape accurately."

checks.text: The blank extends past the traced line on every side, leaving margin material outside the line for cutting and filing.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "a piece of sheet metal larger than the opening"; margin needed for later cut-outside-the-line step.

checks.text: The blank chosen for the filler is the same gauge and alloy as the original skin.
checks.src: Handbook: "The filler must be of the same gauge and material as the original skin." Gauge verified by micrometer, alloy by stock marking.

checks.text: The blank is held flat and flush against the underside of the skin throughout tracing, without tilt or lift.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "against the underside, pressing it flush"; only observable while the trace is made.

errors.text: Blank shifts or is held off the skin, so the traced outline is offset and the finished filler fits loose with excessive gap.
Wrong stock traced — doubler-gauge or different alloy used for the filler instead of skin-gauge material.
Broad or repeated marker lines, or trace run off the blank edge leaving no cutting margin on one side.

steps.text: Remove and cut out the shape.

checks.text: The cut edge lies entirely outside the traced outline, with the marker line still visible on the blank.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note: cut close to the marked line, leaving a small amount of material outside the line.

checks.text: Excess material left outside the traced line is small and reasonably uniform, filable to fit without reworking the whole edge.
checks.src: 'Small amount of material outside the line' is qualitative; the actual margin must be measured off the blank.

checks.text: Cut edges are free of tears, cracks, curl or buckling, and no nick crosses inside the outline.
checks.src: Handbook p.4-93: damage 'must be cleaned and smoothed'; p.4-92 'Smooth out any abrasions and/or dents.'

checks.text: The blank was cut from stock of the same gauge and alloy as the original skin.
checks.src: Handbook: 'The filler must be of the same gauge and material as the original skin.' Verified by micrometer/stock marking, not by sight.

errors.text: Cut runs inside the traced line, producing an undersized filler with a gap around the opening.
Filler blank cut from thinner or dissimilar stock than the skin, which still looks correct once fitted.
Shear or snips leave a curled, torn or work-hardened edge on the blank.

steps.text: Size material to fit the shape.

checks.text: The filler seats fully in the opening and sits flush with the surrounding skin, with no step, lip, or bulge.
checks.src: Handbook: "A flush patch is a filler patch that is flush to the skin when applied"; p.4-93 requires "a smooth outside surface".

checks.text: The gap between filler and opening edge is uniform around the full perimeter, with no wedge-shaped or crescent gap.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: file "until the patch fits the opening"; handbook speaks only qualitatively of fit and contour.

checks.text: Filed edges are straight and square to the surface, free of file gouges, waviness, and burrs.
checks.src: Procedure sheet step 4 deburr/smooth; handbook p.4-92 "Smooth out any abrasions and/or dents" and "Round all square corners".

checks.text: The filler material is the same gauge and alloy as the original skin after fitting.
checks.src: Handbook: "The filler must be of the same gauge and material as the original skin." Verify with micrometer/material marking.

checks.text: The filler enters the opening by hand without forcing, hammering, or rocking in place.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note: file "carefully remove material until the patch fits the opening" — fit judged during trial fitting.

errors.text: Over-filing leaves an oversized, loose filler with a wide or uneven gap that cannot be riveted flush.
Oversized filler forced into the opening, upsetting the skin edge or standing proud of the surface while looking seated.
File chatter, gouges, or burrs left on the filler edges after sizing.

steps.text: Deburr edges and smooth scratches with sandpaper.

checks.text: All cut edges and hole edges of the filler are burr-free and uniformly smooth, with no sharp or ragged sections.
checks.src: Procedure sheet step 4 and safety note 1 (cut/formed metal leaves sharp edges); handbook defines burr as 'a small, thin section of metal extending beyond a regular surface'.

checks.text: No coarse file marks or deep scratches remain on the filler faces or edges after final sanding.
checks.src: Handbook p.4-89: 'Scratches, which penetrate the pure aluminum surface layer, permit corrosion to take place in the alloy beneath.'

checks.text: After sanding, the filler still fits the opening with a uniform gap and no oversize slop from removed material.
checks.src: Procedure sheet Create the Patch Filler note 3: file 'until the patch fits the opening'; fit gap must be gauged, not eyeballed.

checks.text: Filler thickness is unchanged by face sanding and still matches the original skin gauge.
checks.src: Handbook: 'The filler must be of the same gauge and material as the original skin.' Requires micrometer reading.

errors.text: Faces sanded aggressively, thinning the filler below original skin gauge while the part still looks correct.
Burrs or sharp slivers left on the filler edges, preventing flush seating and posing a cut hazard.
Edges over-sanded, enlarging the filler-to-opening gap so the filler no longer fits snugly and must be remade.
Coarse-grit cross scratches left on the clad surface without progression to fine grit.

subtasks.excluded: 6 [measurement], 3 [document] — held beside the frame, never folded into the criterion.

steps.text: Choose the rivet for the repair.

checks.text: Selected rivet diameter equals the next standard size above three times the measured skin thickness.
checks.src: Handbook: "multiply the thickness of the skin by three and use the next larger size rivet corresponding to that figure"; procedure sheet only says "calculate".

checks.text: Rivet type and material match the original rivets in the part being repaired.
checks.src: Handbook: "the rivet size and material should be the same as the original rivets in the part being repaired."

checks.text: Rivet length provides grip for the full doubler-plus-skin-plus-filler stack with enough shank left to upset a shop head.
checks.src: Procedure sheet note: "Calculate the required rivet diameter and length." No numeric length rule appears in the handbook extract.

checks.text: Selected rivet head style (universal or countersunk) matches the existing rivet heads in the surrounding skin.
checks.src: Rests on handbook "the rivet size and material should be the same as the original rivets"; head style comparison is visually settleable.

errors.text: Diameter computed from skin thickness but rounded down instead of up, leaving the joint critical in shear.
Rivet length chosen for skin alone, ignoring doubler and filler gauges, so no shank remains to form a full shop head.
Rivet alloy or head style substituted for what is on hand rather than matching the original installation.

steps.text: Determine and plot the edge distance.

checks.text: Edge distance lines are marked on all four edges of the doubler, the filler, and the skin repair area.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note: "Mark that distance from all edges with a marker"; handbook is qualitative on layout.

checks.text: Each marked edge distance measures the value calculated for the selected rivet diameter, and no less.
checks.src: Handbook: "the proper edge distance for the larger rivet must be maintained"; the numeric value comes from the student's calculation.

checks.text: Marked edge distance meets the handbook minimum for the rivet size used, e.g. 1/4" for 1/8" rivets.
checks.src: Figure 4-175 text: "Minimum edge distance using 1/8" rivets is 1/4" and using 5/32" rivets is 5/16"" (stated for lap/scab patch).

checks.text: Each line runs parallel to its edge at a constant offset, and lines meet cleanly at the corners.
checks.src: Layout must be usable for pitch plotting; handbook only requires patterns "conform to instructions in the applicable aircraft manual".

checks.text: Rivet diameter used in the edge distance calculation matches the rivet chosen in step 1 of the layout.
checks.src: Perform Rivet Layout notes 1-2 require the calculated diameter to drive the edge distance figure.

errors.text: Edge distance marked smaller than the calculated minimum, inviting tearout while the layout still looks orderly.
Edge distance lines omitted on one or more edges, or plotted on only one of the three pieces.
Lines wander or taper relative to the edge, or are drawn with a broad marker that obscures the true dimension.

steps.text: Determine the pitch and plot each rivet.

checks.text: Adjacent dots along each rivet line are spaced at the calculated pitch, equal to one another within layout tolerance.
checks.src: Sheet: "Calculate the needed pitch. Mark a dot at that interval on each material"; requires scale reading between dots.

checks.text: The plotted pitch and rivet count match the documented calculation and the applicable manual's rivet pattern.
checks.src: Handbook p.4-92: "The rivet pattern for a repair must conform to instructions in the applicable aircraft manual"; count from Figure 4-169.

checks.text: Every dot sits on the previously plotted edge-distance lines, with rows symmetrical about the opening and none outside the layout.
checks.src: Sheet step 2 plots edge distance first; dots must fall on those lines for a valid pattern.

checks.text: On a lap or scab patch layout, rows are staggered about 1/2 inch apart with spacing about 1 inch.
checks.src: Handbook: "Space rivets aproximately 1" apart in staggered rows 1/2" apart"; applies to lap/scab patch geometry only.

errors.text: Pitch calculated too large, plotting fewer rivets than the joint needs, leaving a shear-critical repair that looks correct.
Pitch too small, crowding dots so holes will tear out or crack between rivets.
Dots plotted on only one piece, or offset between skin, doubler and filler so patterns cannot align.
Fat, smeared or doubled marker dots that hide the true rivet center.

subtasks.label: Drill the Holes
subtasks.excluded: 11 [measurement], 5 [video] — held beside the frame, never folded into the criterion.

steps.text: Center punch the holes in the skin.

checks.text: Every plotted rivet mark on the skin carries exactly one punch indentation centered on the mark, with no stray or doubled indentations.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Notes: "Place the point of the center punch directly on a mark for a rivet" and "Repeat for all rivet mark locations on the skin."

checks.text: Measured punch-center locations match the plotted edge distance and pitch for the repair layout.
checks.src: Handbook: "The rivet pattern for a repair must conform to instructions in the applicable aircraft manual"; procedure sheet plots ED and pitch marks.

checks.text: The skin around each indentation remains flat, with no warping, dishing or backside bulge from an over-heavy blow.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note: "One light blow is enough; too heavy and the metal will warp"; verify with straightedge/flatness check.

checks.text: The punch is held perpendicular and steady against the skin and struck with a single light hammer blow.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Notes: "Hold the punch steady against the material" and "Lightly tap the top of the center punch".

errors.text: Indentation set off the layout mark, so the drilled hole ends up short of minimum edge distance while looking normal.
Hammer blow too heavy, warping or denting the skin around the punch marks.
Missed or duplicated punch marks, or stray indentations and scratches outside the layout.

steps.text: Drill pilot holes through the marks.

checks.text: Each pilot hole is centered on its center-punch mark, with layout dots still visible around the hole rim.
checks.src: Sheet directs the bit apex be positioned in the punch indentation and holes drilled through the marks, preserving edge distance and pitch.

checks.text: Pilot holes are round and clean, with no elongation, ovalling, tearing or crescent gouging at the hole edge.
checks.src: Handbook: "Drill bits that do not cut satisfactorily cause damage to the hole."

checks.text: Pilot bit diameter is no larger than the rivet diameter, #40 (0.098") for a 1/8" rivet.
checks.src: Sheet: bit "same size as or slightly smaller than the rivet diameter... #40 drill bits are preferred"; handbook gives no such figure.

checks.text: Drill is held perpendicular with the part clamped or backed while drilling, and exit is controlled at breakout.
checks.src: Sheet: keep drill perpendicular, anticipate exit; handbook mentions clamping and a wood support only in the titanium hand-drilling context.

errors.text: Pilot drilled with a bit larger than the rivet diameter, leaving an oversize hole no step-up can correct.
Holes drilled off the punch marks, breaking edge distance or pitch on skin, doubler or filler.
Drill wanders or is skewed, producing elongated, triangular or torn holes and back-side breakout damage.
Chuck or bit contact scratches and mars the skin around the holes at breakout.

steps.text: Drill the patch doubler.

checks.text: Every drilled doubler hole is concentric with its mating skin hole, with cleco pins seated fully and no crescent or double-drilled openings.
checks.src: Sheet: 'Transfer holes from the skin to the doubler... Drill a hole and hold it aligned with a cleco pin.'

checks.text: The doubler is held with cleco clamps or pins so it cannot shift between the first and last hole drilled.
checks.src: Sheet: 'Secure in place with cleco clamps, if possible'; only observable while drilling progresses.

checks.text: Hole centers on the doubler sit at the laid-out edge distance from the doubler edges, with the ED line bisecting the transferred skin holes.
checks.src: Sheet: 'Bisect the holes in the skin with the edge distance line on the doubler.' Handbook only states edge distance 'must be maintained' qualitatively.

checks.text: Pilot holes are drilled with a bit no larger than the rivet diameter (#40 preferred for a 1/8" rivet).
checks.src: Sheet note 6: bit 'same size as or slightly smaller than the rivet diameter... #40 drill bits are preferred'; figure is the sheet's alone.

errors.text: Doubler shifts while drilling, so holes only line up when forced with a cleco, leaving elongated holes hidden between the layers.
Doubler drilled with too little edge margin, so a hole breaks out or leaves insufficient edge distance for riveting.
Drill held off perpendicular, producing angled or oval holes and burred breakout on the back face of the doubler.

steps.text: Drill the patch filler.

checks.text: Every hole in the filler is round and full-size, with no teardrop, elongation or double-drilled crescent.
checks.src: Handbook warns of "holes that have been elongated" and "if the rivet holes show elongation, replace the rivets with the next larger size" (p.4-91/4-92).

checks.text: Filler holes hold the laid-out edge distance and pitch from every filler edge.
checks.src: Procedure sheet requires plotted ED and pitch; handbook only states "The rivet pattern for a repair must conform to instructions in the applicable aircraft manual" (p.4-92).

checks.text: Filler sits in the opening flush with the skin and its holes register with the doubler on cleco pins.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: fit into opening and transfer holes to doubler; handbook: "A flush patch is a filler patch that is flush to the skin" (p.4-96).

checks.text: Filler shows no warp, dishing or bulge around the punched and drilled holes.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note: "One light blow is enough; too heavy and the metal will warp"; handbook lists upsetting as a defect (p.4-90).

checks.text: Drill is held perpendicular with the filler clamped or backed while drilling.
checks.src: Procedure sheet note 12; handbook: "When hand drilling thin or flexible parts, put a support (such as a block of wood) behind the part" (p.4-85).

errors.text: Drill wandered or was tilted, producing an oversize/teardrop hole that a rivet head will later hide.
Filler holes drilled short of the required edge distance, inviting tear-out while looking acceptable.
Filler holes miss the doubler layout, so transferred holes are mismatched and the filler will not sit flush.
Heavy center punch blow or drill grab dished the filler around a hole.

steps.text: Step up to the next drill bit size.

checks.text: The final hole diameter is at least 0.003 in larger than the rivet diameter (e.g. #30, 0.1285 in, for a -4 rivet).
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note 17 gives the ream dimension; handbook pages speak only qualitatively about hole size and rivet fit.

checks.text: The step-up sequence is pilot #40 then finish size, with no size skipped past the specified increment.
checks.src: Notes 6 and 17 fix pilot (#40) and finish (#30) bits; handbook increments (0.0313/0.0625 in) apply only to titanium holes 0.1875 in and larger.

checks.text: Finished holes are round and clean, with no elongation, tearing or triangular lobing at the hole edge.
checks.src: "Drill bits that do not cut satisfactorily cause damage to the hole"; p.4-91 warns of "holes that have been elongated."

checks.text: Skin, doubler and filler remain clamped or clecoed together while holes are enlarged, so the stack stays aligned.
checks.src: Handbook: "clamp them together tightly... use temporary bolts, Cleco clamps" (stated for titanium hand drilling); procedure notes 14-16 require cleco pins.

checks.text: The new bit is chucked with the flutes fully exposed clear of the chuck jaws.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note 7: "Install drill bit into pneumatic drill with flutes fully exposed."

errors.text: Holes left at pilot size or under the ream dimension, so rivets are forced into interference and shanks are damaged.
Bit size skipped or oversized bit used, enlarging holes beyond ream dimension and leaving a loose fit that looks normal once riveted.
Clecos removed during step-up, letting the stack shift so enlarged holes are misaligned or elongated.
Excessive feed or dull bit leaves torn, out-of-round holes and heavy burrs on the exit side.

steps.text: Drill all holes up to the finished size.

checks.text: Each finished hole measures at least 0.003" larger than the rivet diameter (e.g., 0.1285"/#30 for a -4 rivet).
checks.src: Procedure sheet Senior Mechanic Note 17 gives the ream dimension; handbook pages supplied state no such figure.

checks.text: Finished holes are round and clean-edged, with no elongation, tri-lobing or torn bore walls.
checks.src: "Drill bits that do not cut satisfactorily cause damage to the hole"; p.4-91 treats elongated holes as defects.

checks.text: Holes remain concentric through skin, doubler and filler with no step or crescent between layers.
checks.src: Handbook treats "holes in the sheet misaligned" as a defect condition; procedure sheet requires cleco pinning to hold alignment.

checks.text: Edge distance to the plotted layout lines is still met after enlarging holes to finished size.
checks.src: "the proper edge distance for the larger rivet must be maintained" when a hole is enlarged.

errors.text: Holes left at pilot/#40 size so rivets must be forced, damaging the hole while the work looks finished.
Layers shift because clecos were removed before final drilling, leaving offset holes hidden between skin, doubler and filler.
Drill wander or non-perpendicular drilling leaves oversized, elongated or tri-lobed holes.

steps.text: Deburr all drilled holes from both sides.

checks.text: No raised metal or burr ring remains around any drilled hole on either face of skin, doubler and filler.
checks.src: Sheet: "Deburr all drilled holes from both sides." Handbook only defines a burr as "a small, thin section of metal extending beyond a regular surface... on the edge of a hole."

checks.text: Hole diameter after deburring is still at the finished/ream size and not enlarged or knife-edged by the deburr tool.
checks.src: Sheet: ream "at least 0.003" larger than the rivet diameter" (e.g., #30 = 0.1285" for a -4 rivet); handbook gives no deburr dimension.

checks.text: Parts were separated so the faying (hidden) faces of every hole were deburred, not just the exposed sides.
checks.src: "from both sides" — the blind face cannot be verified once the assembly is re-clecoed.

checks.text: Faying surfaces and hole edges are free of chips, shavings and FOD before reassembly.
checks.src: Sheet equipment list includes FOD box; trapped swarf prevents parts sitting flush.

errors.text: Only the accessible face is deburred; burrs on the mating faces hold the sheets apart while the assembly still looks flush and correct.

subtasks.label: Set up Rivet Gun
subtasks.excluded: 2 [measurement], 3 [video] — held beside the frame, never folded into the criterion.

steps.text: Choose the set and spring.

checks.text: The selected set's tip style matches the rivet head style to be driven — concave recess for universal, flat disk for countersunk.
checks.src: Sheet: universal set has 'concave recess on tip'; countersunk set has 'disk-shaped head'. Handbook extract does not cover rivet gun sets.

checks.text: The concave recess diameter equals the rivet head diameter, neither undersized nor oversized.
checks.src: Sheet requires recess 'the same size as rivet head'; sizing needs a measured or gauged comparison, not appearance.

checks.text: The retaining spring form matches the chosen set — cone-shaped for a universal set, cylindrical for a countersunk set.
checks.src: Sheet: universal 'uses a cone-shaped retaining spring'; countersunk 'uses a cylinder shaped retaining spring'.

checks.text: Set shank and spring are undamaged, clean and free of burrs, mushrooming or chipping on the working face.
checks.src: Implied by sheet's set selection step; a marred set face transfers defects to rivet heads. Needs SME confirmation of acceptance limit.

errors.text: A flat countersunk set is chosen for universal-head rivets (or a concave set for flush rivets), deforming heads and skin.
Spring form does not match the set, so the set is not retained and can be ejected from the gun in use.
Set recess is oversized for the rivet head, letting the set slip and mark the skin with 'smiles'.

steps.text: Install the set and spring on the rivet gun.

checks.text: The retaining spring is threaded fully onto the gun barrel with no exposed threads or gap at the collar.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "Slide the spring over the set down to the threads" and rotate gun in tightening direction.

checks.text: The installed set matches the rivet type: concave recess with cone-shaped spring for universal, disk head with cylindrical spring for countersunk.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note distinguishes universal (concave recess, cone spring) from countersunk (disk head, cylinder spring) setups.

checks.text: The concave recess diameter of the set equals the rivet head size being driven.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note: recess "the same size as rivet head"; requires comparing set recess to rivet head dimension.

checks.text: The spring is tightened until a marked rise in torque is felt and the set is captive in the gun.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: rotate "until you feel a high rise in torque"; tactile and retention cannot be seen in a still.

errors.text: Spring only hand-started, not torqued down, so the set can be ejected from the gun under recoil.
Wrong set installed for the rivet head type (disk set on universal rivets), which will mar the head and skin.
Set installed with concave head reversed or spring cross-threaded on the barrel.

steps.text: Set rivet gun pressure.

checks.text: The rivet gun is connected to a compressed air source with the hose secured at the gun inlet.
checks.src: Sheet: "Connect the gun to a source of compressed air"; handbook pages 4-85..4-96 do not address rivet gun pressure setup.

checks.text: The set tip is pressed into a scrap wood block, not the workpiece or an installed rivet, while pressure is set.
checks.src: Sheet: "Moderately press the set head into a block of wood. Keep it there while setting pressure."

checks.text: The trigger is pulled fully while the regulator is twisted, and the set stays captive in the gun throughout.
checks.src: Sheet: "Pull the trigger fully while twisting the regulator"; retaining spring must hold set during firing.

checks.text: Regulator is adjusted off maximum to a recoil the student can control without the gun walking off the block.
checks.src: Sheet: "twisting the regulator until a manageable recoil is found"; no psi value given by either source.

errors.text: Gun fired free in the air or with set unrestrained, launching the set as a projectile.
Pressure set by firing against the actual skin or a rivet, denting the repair while the gun looks correctly rigged.
Regulator left at or near maximum, so first rivets are driven with uncontrollable recoil.
Trigger feathered instead of pulled fully, so the recoil judged does not represent driving conditions.

steps.text: Insert a rivet.

checks.text: The rivet passes through every layer to be joined (skin, doubler, and filler as applicable), with its shank visible on the far side.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note 1: "Press a rivet through all the sheets of material to be joined."

checks.text: The manufactured head is fully seated against the skin with no gap or cocking between head and sheet.
checks.src: Procedure sheet requires the rivet head be kept flush to the skin; a seated head is the inspectable outcome of insertion.

checks.text: The rivet installed matches the diameter, length, and material determined in the rivet-layout step for this repair.
checks.src: Handbook p.4-92: "Normally, the rivet size and material should be the same as the original rivets in the part being repaired." Procedure sheet: calculate rivet diameter and length.

checks.text: Protruding shank length is sufficient to form a shop head of about 0.5D height and 1.5D width.
checks.src: Shop head 0.5D/1.5D is the procedure sheet's figure alone; handbook extract states no protrusion value. Needs SME confirmation of pre-buck protrusion.

checks.text: The sheets are held in contact at the rivet location, with no visible gap or slippage between layers before bucking.
checks.src: Insertion must not spring the layers apart; procedure sheet directs clecoing/holding parts aligned during fastening.

errors.text: Rivet inserted through only some layers (e.g., misses the filler or doubler), leaving a joint that looks riveted but carries no load path.
Undersized or wrong-material rivet dropped into an oversize hole, loose in the bore yet plausible-looking once bucked.
Rivet too short, leaving insufficient shank to form a full shop head.
Head left unseated or cocked in the hole, or the rivet falls out before the gun is applied.

steps.text: Align the rivet gun.

checks.text: The rivet set is seated squarely on the manufactured head, fully covering it with no offset onto the surrounding skin.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "Press the rivet set snug into the rivet head." Concentric seating is visible in a still of the held position.

checks.text: The gun barrel axis is held perpendicular to the skin and stays perpendicular through the recoil.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "Keep the rivet gun perpendicular to the material and stabilize your wrist to control the recoil"; a still cannot show it was held.

checks.text: The skin and manufactured head around the rivet are free of set marks, gouges or deformities from off-axis contact.
checks.src: Handbook: "examining both the shop and manufactured heads and the surrounding skin and structural parts for deformities."

checks.text: The rivet shank remains straight and unjoggled in the hole after the set is aligned and pressure applied.
checks.src: Handbook: "Joggles in removed rivet shanks indicate partial shear failure"; joggling is only evidenced as it occurs, not from a surface still.

errors.text: Gun held off-axis so the set drives the rivet crooked, joggling the shank inside a joint that still looks acceptable outside.
Set not pressed snug or not centered on the head, so it skids onto the skin and gouges or 'smiles' the surface.
Wrist not stabilized, letting the gun walk under recoil and leaving scuffs or a tipped manufactured head.

steps.text: Position the bucking bar.

checks.text: The bucking bar's hardened flat face sits squarely and fully centered on the rivet shank, not overhanging onto the surrounding skin.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "Place its hardened surface on the rivet shank directly in line with the rivet gun set." Handbook extract is silent on bucking bar use.

checks.text: The contact face of the bucking bar is smooth and free of nicks, burrs or paint that would mark the shop head.
checks.src: Implied by requirement to use the bar's "hardened surface" against the shank; damaged faces transfer defects to the shop head.

checks.text: The bar stays coaxial with the gun set and perpendicular to the sheet for the whole burst, without walking off the shank.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: keep the bucking bar perpendicular "to avoid joggling the rivet shank"; only observable while driving.

checks.text: The bar is held firmly against the material with pull pressure matching the gun's push, so it does not bounce clear.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "Equal the pushing pressure on the rivet gun with the pulling pressure on the bucking bar."

errors.text: Bar offset or cocked on the shank, clinching the shank sideways so the shop head forms off-center yet still looks formed.
Bar allowed to bounce or lift during driving, leaving an under-driven, loose rivet that appears seated.
Bar edge or face strikes the skin beside the rivet, denting or scarring the repair area.

steps.text: Buck the rivet.

checks.text: The manufactured head sits flush against the skin with no gap, tipping, or raised edge around it.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "Keep the rivet head flush to the skin." Handbook only addresses head slippage on removed/existing rivets.

checks.text: The shop head is concentric with the shank and not clinched, cocked, or joggled to one side.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "Keep the bucking bar perpendicular to avoid joggling the rivet shank." Handbook discusses joggled shanks only for removed rivets.

checks.text: Skin and doubler around the rivet are free of bucking bar dents, set 'smileys,' and upset material.
checks.src: Follows from procedure sheet's flush-head and controlled, equalized pressure requirement; no handbook figure applies to this step.

checks.text: Gun and bucking bar are held perpendicular with pushing and pulling pressure equalized for a 1–3 second trigger pull.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "Pull the trigger all the way for 1 to 3 seconds" and equal pushing/pulling pressure; only visible while performed.

checks.text: Any rivet head cracking stays within limits: depth under 1/8 and width under 1/16 of shank diameter.
checks.src: Handbook: "The depth of the crack is less than 1/8 of the shank diameter"; "width of the crack is less than 1/16 of the shank diameter."

errors.text: Bucking bar held off-line, producing a clinched or joggled shank with a cocked shop head that still looks set.
Rivet over-driven — shop head flattened beyond limits, skin dimpled and hole enlarged around the rivet.
Bucking bar or rivet set slips, leaving 'smiley' crescent marks or dents in the skin.

steps.text: Check the shop head dimensions.

checks.text: Measured shop head height is approximately 0.5 × rivet shank diameter.
checks.src: Procedure sheet note 5: 'preferred height = 0.5D'; the cited handbook pages give no shop head dimensions.

checks.text: Measured shop head width (diameter) is approximately 1.5 × rivet shank diameter.
checks.src: Procedure sheet note 5: 'preferred width = 1.5D'; handbook extract states no numeric shop head standard.

checks.text: Shop head is round and concentric on the shank, not clinched, tipped or joggled to one side.
checks.src: Handbook p.4-91: 'examining both the shop and manufactured heads and the surrounding skin and structural parts for deformities'; sheet says keep bar perpendicular 'to avoid joggling'.

checks.text: Manufactured head sits flush with the skin and surrounding skin shows no dishing, smiles or gaps between sheets.
checks.src: Sheet: 'Keep the rivet head flush to the skin.' Handbook p.4-91 requires inspecting 'the surrounding skin and structural parts for deformities'.

errors.text: Under-driven rivet accepted: shop head shorter/narrower than 1.5D width, still looks formed to a novice.
Bucking bar held off-axis, producing a clinched or joggled shop head that will not carry shear.
Over-driven rivet: shop head flattened past 0.5D height with cracking or skin dished around the head.

subtasks.label: Remove the Rivet
subtasks.excluded: 3 [video], 8 [measurement] — held beside the frame, never folded into the criterion.

steps.text: Center punch the rivet head.

checks.text: A single punch indentation sits at the geometric center of the rivet head, not offset toward its edge.
checks.src: Sheet note 1: 'Place the point of the center punch in the middle of the rivet head.'

checks.text: The rivet head and surrounding skin show no dishing, dent or upset metal from the hammer blow.
checks.src: Sheet: 'Lightly tap'; handbook defines 'Dent—indentation in a metal surface produced by an object striking with force... surrounding... slightly upset.'

checks.text: No stray punch marks, slip scratches or hammer strikes appear on the skin around the target rivet.
checks.src: Handbook: 'Scratch—slight tear or break in metal surface from light, momentary contact'; sheet requires punch held on the rivet head only.

checks.text: The indentation is deep enough to seat the drill point so the bit does not walk off the head.
checks.src: Purpose of the punch mark per sheet sequence; only evidenced by the punch/drill start being performed.

checks.text: The punch was struck with one light blow, the punch held steady and perpendicular to the head.
checks.src: Sheet note 1: 'Lightly tap the punch with a hammer.'

errors.text: Punch mark placed off-center on the rivet head, so the subsequent drill cuts into the skin or enlarges the hole.
Blow too heavy, denting the rivet head and warping or upsetting the surrounding skin.
Punch slips off the head, leaving stray marks or scratches in the skin.

steps.text: Drill into the rivet head.

checks.text: The drilled hole is centered in the rivet head, concentric with the head and not encroaching on the surrounding skin.
checks.src: Follows from centering the punch in the middle of the rivet head so the drill stays within the head.

checks.text: The drill bit used is smaller in diameter than the rivet shank diameter.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: 'Use a drill bit smaller than the diameter of the rivet'; handbook gives no bit size here.

checks.text: Drilling depth stops at the bottom of the rivet head and does not extend into the shank or underlying structure.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: 'only drill down to the bottom of the rivet head'; handbook p.4-91: 'drilling off the head and carefully punching out the shank'.

checks.text: The skin around the rivet head shows no drill gouging, chatter marks, or elongation of the rivet hole.
checks.src: Handbook: 'carefully punching out the shank' and warns 'if the rivet holes show elongation, replace the rivets with the next larger size'.

errors.text: Drilling straight through the head into the shank and hole, elongating or oversizing the rivet hole while still looking normal.
Using a bit equal to or larger than the rivet diameter, cutting the hole oversize so the original rivet size can no longer be used.
Drill walks off-center and gouges or cuts the surrounding skin around the rivet head.

steps.text: Remove the rivet head.

checks.text: The rivet head is completely sheared free of the shank, with no partial collar or attached fragment remaining.
checks.src: Sheet requires rolling the punch to 'shear off the rivet head'; handbook speaks only of 'drilling off the head'.

checks.text: The skin around the rivet shows no punch gouges, crescent scoring, or new dents from the shearing action.
checks.src: Handbook: rivets are removed 'by drilling off the head and carefully punching out the shank'; careless punching marks the sheet.

checks.text: The punch used is smaller in diameter than the hole drilled in the rivet head.
checks.src: Sheet: 'Insert a smaller diameter punch than the drilled hole in the rivet head.'

checks.text: The skin hole remains round and to nominal diameter, not elongated or stretched by the punch.
checks.src: Handbook: 'if the rivet holes show elongation, replace the rivets with the next larger size' — elongation needs gauging, not sight.

errors.text: An oversize punch or hammer blows are used, shearing the head but expanding or elongating the skin hole while the work still looks normal.
The head is only partly sheared and is pried or chiselled off, gouging and denting the surrounding skin.
The punch slips off the drilled recess and leaves scratches or a shallow ring mark around the rivet.

steps.text: Punch out the rivet shank.

checks.text: The hole is completely clear of rivet material, with the freed shank present as a separate piece.
checks.src: Step calls for the shank knocked through the hole; a residual plug or partial shank means the step is unfinished.

checks.text: The punch used is equal to, not larger than, the rivet diameter.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note 4: 'Use a punch equal to the rivet diameter to knock it through the hole.'

checks.text: The vacated hole is still round and to original size, with no elongation from the punch.
checks.src: Handbook p.4-91: 'if the rivet holes show elongation, replace the rivets with the next larger size'; gauge hole in two axes.

checks.text: The skin around the hole is free of punch strikes, dents or dishing from the removal.
checks.src: Handbook p.4-91: shank is to be 'carefully punching out'; surrounding skin must show no new distortion.

checks.text: The workpiece was backed/supported so the blow drove the shank out rather than deflecting the sheet.
checks.src: Handbook p.4-85: 'When hand drilling thin or flexible parts, put a support (such as a block of wood) behind the part' — same principle applied to punching.

errors.text: An oversize punch is driven through, enlarging or ovaling the hole while the surface still looks clean.
Shank is only partly driven and remains lodged in the hole, hidden from the visible side.
Hammering on an unsupported panel dishes or dents the skin around the hole.

steps.text: Inspect the hole for damage.

checks.text: The vacated hole is round and free of elongation, tearout or cracks running from its edge.
checks.src: Procedure: "Look for irregular hole shapes." Handbook: "if the rivet holes show elongation, replace the rivets with the next larger size"; "Sheet failures, such as tearouts, cracks between rivets."

checks.text: Hole diameter matches the original nominal rivet hole size, with no enlargement beyond it.
checks.src: "If a rivet hole has been enlarged or deformed, the next larger size rivet must be used after reworking the hole." Enlargement is only settled by gauging.

checks.text: Skin around the hole is free of drill or punch gouges, scoring and raised burrs on both faces.
checks.src: Damage Removal: "Smooth out any abrasions and/or dents"; burr defined p.4-90 as metal "on the edge of a hole."

checks.text: If the hole is enlarged or deformed, edge distance still meets minimum for the next larger rivet.
checks.src: "the proper edge distance for the larger rivet must be maintained" — requires a dimension from hole centre to edge.

errors.text: An elongated or out-of-round hole is judged serviceable and re-riveted with the same size rivet, hiding a bearing failure.
Hole is torn or crescent-gouged oversize by the punch or drill wandering off the rivet head.
Burrs and drill swarf left at the hole edge, so the inspection is made through obscuring debris.
